The support FAQ, product guide, and customer interviews collectively describe scanned PDF handling as a major ingestion challenge because scanned PDFs are image-only and lack a searchable text layer.

- **OCR is required.** The support FAQ states scanned PDFs require Optical Character Recognition (OCR); without OCR they cannot be searched and citations cannot be generated, because the standard parser only reads digital text layers and extracts zero text from image-only scans [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. The product guide similarly lists PDF as the default format but notes that scanned/image-only PDFs require OCR processing, with citation precision at page/paragraph level [NL-002#NL-002-S08].

- **OCR failures cause real downstream problems.** The FAQ warns that OCR is heuristic: blurry, low-resolution, handwritten, or complex-layout scans can produce misread characters or broken paragraphs, leading to broken citations, knowledge gaps, and longer processing times [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. Customer interviews confirm this: ingestion/OCR issues were the largest support category at 112 of 412 tickets (27%) in May 2026, with 40–50% of enterprise files being scanned PDFs; TutorChat either returned no citations or pointed to the whole document, and CSAT dropped from 4.5 to 3.8 [NL-021#NL-021-S02]. BrightPath reported ~45% of its corpus was image-only scans causing missing or page-1-of-150 citations [NL-024#NL-024-S04]. A clinician described a scanned ventilator protocol where OCR/extraction failure omitted critical alarm threshold steps, creating a safety risk [NL-018#NL-018-S05]. Another customer described having to manually run OCR before uploading legacy SOP scans [NL-017#NL-017-S06].

- **Recommended mitigations.** The FAQ advises checking upload metadata and OCR enablement, inspecting scan quality, exporting native text-searchable PDFs from source systems, using the Advanced OCR Pipeline (Enterprise or Growth add-on) for scans, converting tables to CSV/XLSX or formatting them with clear dark grid lines, and transcribing handwriting into digital text [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. The BrightPath discussion recommends uploading original DOCX/text files instead of scans and, for the pilot, excluding scans from the active corpus until the Advanced OCR Pipeline is available [NL-024#NL-024-S04]. Customers also want automated OCR inside KnowledgeHub rather than manual pre-processing [NL-017#NL-017-S06].

- **Planned solution.** The Advanced OCR Pipeline is targeted for release in August 2026 and will automatically detect image-only PDFs, extract text and layout structures, and enable page-specific citations [NL-024#NL-024-S04] [NL-018#NL-018-S05] [NL-017#NL-017-S06]. Clinical customers additionally want validation controls, such as a review interface showing original scans side-by-side with extracted text and low-confidence character highlighting, to catch dangerous OCR misreads like medication doses [NL-018#NL-018-S05]. Engineering planning also includes split queues and OCR-specific caps, e.g., capping Starter at 100 pages, Growth at 500 pages, and Enterprise at 2,000 pages per scanned document [NL-021#NL-021-S06].
